rationale: Clinical characterization across the literature consistently delineates KLHL20-related neurodevelopmental disorder with early-onset seizures, facial dysmorphism, and behavioral abnormalities (NEDSFBA, OMIM #621390) as a non-degenerative neurodevelopmental syndrome. Affected individuals present in early life with febrile seizures or infantile epileptic encephalopathies (including infantile spasms / West syndrome), alongside developmental delay. Follow-up into childhood and adolescence demonstrates persistent intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder, and hyperactivity as the primary persistent disabilities, rather than the relentless loss of acquired milestones characteristic of neurodegenerative disorders.

evidence.text: Sleyp et al. (2022) established that de novo missense variants in KLHL20 cause a static neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by intellectual disability, febrile seizures or epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder, hyperactivity, and subtle facial dysmorphisms, without evidence of neurodegenerative decline.

source.quote: We studied 14 patients with de novo missense variants in KLHL20, delineating a genetic syndrome with patients having mild to severe intellectual disability, febrile seizures or epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder, hyperactivity, and subtle dysmorphic facial features. We observed a recurrent de novo missense variant in 11 patients (NM_014458.4:c.1069G>A p.[Gly357Arg]).

evidence.text: Kuroda et al. (2024) described early-onset epilepsy manifesting as West syndrome associated with a novel KLHL20 variant, confirming that epileptic phenotypes manifest in early infancy against a background of developmental delay.

new_directions.question_text: What is the long-term seizure freedom rate and medication responsiveness in adult KLHL20 mutation carriers?
new_directions.rationale: While early seizures are prominent, natural history data on whether epilepsy spontaneously remits or requires lifelong polytherapy into adulthood in larger patient cohorts remains underdocumented.

new_directions.question_text: Do non-Kelch domain variants or putative loss-of-function variants in KLHL20 present with a different neurodevelopmental or neurodegenerative trajectory than the recurrent Kelch-domain missense variants?
new_directions.rationale: Almost all published individuals harbor missense variants clustered within the Kelch-type beta-propeller domain (notably p.Gly357Arg), leaving open whether other variant classes produce non-concordant natural histories.
